newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Two big investors in WorldCom.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Two big investors in WorldCom.

text.p: A couple of WorldCom Inc options were heavily traded at the Pacific Exchange (PCX) Friay as two investors closed out positions.
The WorldCom September 35 call traded about 13,800 contracts and the January 25 call traded around 6,900.
A market maker in the options said a public customer bought 8,000 of the September 35 calls to close a position and the rest of the trades were from broker-dealers.
"The Jan 25s is a customer selling them out," he said, adding that the customer had been long those options at lower levels.
WorldCom shares ended down 3/4 at 32-3/4 on turnover of roughly 4.1 million shares.

In other activity, options on shares of Electronic Data Systems Corp were active as the stock slid sharply after the company late Thursday said it expected its 1997 earnings to fall below previous expectations.
EDS shares lost 6-1/16 to 37-1/8. It was the most active stock on the New York Stock Exchange, with more than 11.2 million shares changing hands. Consolidated volume topped 14 million shares.
EDS put options drew the most interest as the August 40 put traded 2,485 contracts. The option, which had open interest of 2,998 contracts through Thursday, when 772 were added, rose 2-1/4 to 3-3/8.
The August 42-1/2 puts traded about 2,160. It had open interest of 2,084 and climbed 3-3/4 to 5-5/8.
The August 45 put traded about 1,250 contracts and the September 35 put traded nearly 1,200.
The busiest EDS call was the September 40, which traded about 1,265 contracts. It had open interest of 1,000 contracts and lost 3-5/8 to 1-1/4.
The company's profit warning led to several rating downgrades, including from Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch, Goldman Sachs and Cowen & Co.
